# Element types

Each type has a home on the spine (its `anchors`), the fields, sections and structured blocks it needs, and the rung from which each is required. Fields marked `optional` are never required. Every record also carries the envelope: `id`, `title`, `summary`, `anchor`, `maturity`, `tier`, `approval`, `lifecycle`, `lifecycle_note`, `origin`, `owner`, `tags`, `aliases`, `reviewed`, `links`, `rel`.

## Intent

_Why does this product exist, and what must it achieve?_

### `PROD` Product

The product as a whole: why it exists, who it serves, what it promises and where its edges are.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: nothing: it is the root. One per product.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | string | text | `outlined` | What kind of product this is, in a few words. |
| `stage` | enum | idea \| building \| launched \| growth \| mature \| sunset | `outlined` | Where the product is in its life. |
| `customer_model` | enum | b2b \| b2c \| b2b2c \| marketplace | `outlined` | Who pays and who uses. |
| `platforms` | strings | a list: [item, item] | `specified` | Where it runs: web, ios, android, api, desktop, cli. |
| `markets` | strings | a list: [item, item] | `specified` | Regions, jurisdictions and languages in scope. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Problem | `outlined` | all | What problem does the product solve, for whom, and how severe is it? What do people do today instead? What evidence shows the problem is real? |
| Value proposition | `outlined` | all | What core value is delivered, and what makes it different from the alternatives? Why would people adopt it, and why might they reject it? |
| Business model | `outlined` | all | Who is the customer, the buyer and the user? How does the product earn: revenue model, pricing and packaging, acquisition, retention, main cost drivers? |
| Boundaries | `specified` | all | What is in scope, explicitly out of scope and deliberately deferred? Which external systems does it depend on? Which platforms, markets and jurisdictions are supported? Which constraints and assumptions apply? |
| Success | `specified` | all | What is the north-star outcome? Which activation, retention, revenue and quality measures matter, and which guardrails must not be broken? |
| Direction | `specified` | all | What are the current priorities, what is planned and what is deferred? What would make you change direction? |

### `OBJ` Objective

An outcome the product exists to achieve, stated so that it can be measured. Sub-objectives anchor on their parent.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `PROD`, `OBJ`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | outcome \| business \| guardrail | `outlined` | outcome: a change in user behaviour or result. business: revenue, cost or risk. guardrail: something that must not get worse. |
| `horizon` | string | text | optional | When it should be true, for example 2027-Q2. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intent | `outlined` | all | State the outcome in plain words. Why does it matter, and how will we know we got there? |

### `OPP` Opportunity

A user need, pain or job worth addressing. Sub-opportunities anchor on their parent, forming an opportunity tree.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `PROD`, `OPP`.

**Fields**

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `statement` | text | text | `outlined` | Preferably in job form: When ..., I want to ..., so that ... |
| `kind` | enum | need \| pain \| job \| gain | `outlined` | What sort of opportunity this is. |
| `basis` | enum | research \| assumption | `outlined` | research: backed by evidence records. assumption: a hypothesis, which must have an assumption record. |
| `importance` | enum | low \| medium \| high | `specified` | How much it matters to the people who have it. |
| `satisfaction_today` | enum | low \| medium \| high | `specified` | How well existing alternatives serve it today. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Situation | `outlined` | all | When does the need arise, what triggers it, and what do people do about it today? |

### `PRIN` Principle

A standing rule of judgement that settles recurring design and behaviour choices.

| `statement` | text | text | `outlined` | The principle in one or two sentences. |
| `implication` | text | text | `specified` | What it means in practice when two options conflict. |

## Actors

_Who is involved, and what may each of them do?_

### `ACT` Actor

Anyone or anything that interacts with the product: a person, an automated process or an outside party.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `PROD`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | human \| system \| external | `outlined` | human: a person. system: automation inside the product. external: an outside party or service acting on it. |
| `internal` | bool | true \| false | optional | True for staff of the company that runs the product, false for customer side. |
| `authn` | string | text | optional | How they prove who they are: password, SSO, API key, signed webhook, none. |
| `goals` | strings | a list: [item, item] | optional | What they are trying to get done. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who they are | `outlined` | all | Who or what is this actor, and what is their relationship to the product? |
| Access and lifecycle | `specified` | all | How are they created or invited, activated, given or changed in role, suspended and removed? What happens to their sessions and tokens? |
| Exceptions and security | `specified` | all | What can they do unauthenticated, with expired or revoked access, or with conflicting roles? How is privilege escalation prevented? Is impersonation possible and how is it audited? |

### `PERS` Persona

A research-based picture of a group of people with similar needs and behaviour.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `PROD`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `basis` | enum | research \| assumption | `outlined` | research: built from evidence records. assumption: a hypothesis, which must have an assumption record. |
| `role_title` | string | text | optional | Typical job title or role in life. |
| `goals` | strings | a list: [item, item] | optional | What they are trying to achieve. |
| `frustrations` | strings | a list: [item, item] | optional | What gets in their way today. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Day in the life | `outlined` | all | What does a typical day look like for them, and where does this product fit into it? |

A named bundle of permissions assigned within a scope.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `PROD`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | enum | platform \| account \| workspace \| resource | `outlined` | The context in which the role is held. |
| `assignable_by` | ref | the id of a ROLE | optional | The role that may assign this one. |
| `min_holders` | int | a whole number | optional | The fewest people who must hold it, for example 1 for an owner. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |

### `PERM` Permission

One thing a holder is allowed to do, to one kind of resource.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `PROD`, `DOM`, `CAP`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | string | text | `outlined` | The verb: view, create, send, void, export, invite. |
| `resource` | string | text | `outlined` | What it applies to, in business words. |
| `scope` | enum | self \| workspace \| account \| platform | `outlined` | How far it reaches. |
| `sensitive` | bool | true \| false | optional | True when use must be audit-logged and may need extra verification. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meaning | `outlined` | all | Precisely what does holding this permission allow, and what does it not allow? |

### `TEN` Tenancy model

How customers are separated from one another: what a tenant is, how tenants nest, what is isolated and who pays.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `PROD`. One per product.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unit` | string | text | `outlined` | What a tenant is: account, workspace, organisation. |
| `hierarchy` | strings | a list: [item, item] | `outlined` | The levels, outermost first, for example organisation, workspace, project. |
| `isolation` | enum | row_level \| schema \| database \| hybrid | `specified` | How tenant data is separated. |
| `billing_entity` | string | text | `specified` | Which level is billed. |
| `multi_membership` | bool | true \| false | `specified` | Whether one person can belong to several tenants. |
| `residency` | string | text | optional | Where tenant data may live. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Model | `outlined` | all | What is a tenant, how do tenants nest, and how does a person relate to them? |
| Provisioning | `specified` | all | How is a tenant created and set up, and by whom? |
| Offboarding | `specified` | all | How is a tenant suspended, exported and deleted, and what is kept? |
| Cross-tenant interactions | `specified` | all | Can tenants share anything? How do partners, resellers and support staff act across tenants? |
| Isolation guarantees | `specified` | all | What exactly is guaranteed never to leak between tenants, and how is that enforced and proven? |

## Structure

_What exists?_

### `DOM` Domain

A bounded area of the product with one clear responsibility. Domains nest.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `PROD`, `DOM`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `strategic` | enum | core \| supporting \| generic | `outlined` | core: where the product differentiates. supporting: needed but not differentiating. generic: a solved problem, ideally bought or standard. |
| `responsibility` | string | text | `outlined` | The one thing this domain is responsible for, in one sentence. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Boundaries | `specified` | all | What does this domain own, what does it deliberately not own, and how does it interact with its neighbours? |

### `CAP` Capability

Something the product can do, stated as an ability rather than a screen or a task. Capabilities nest.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `DOM`, `CAP`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tier` | enum | 1 \| 2 \| 3 | `outlined` | Criticality of this capability. |
| `outcome` | string | text | `outlined` | What the people it serves can achieve with it. |
| `owner` | string | text | `specified` | Who is accountable for it. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose and outcome | `outlined` | all | What can people do with this capability that they could not before, and why does it matter? |
| Scope | `specified` | all | What is inside and outside this capability, and which neighbouring capabilities does it rely on? |

### `FEAT` Feature

A deliverable behaviour that realises a capability. Its flows, screens, rules, requirements and tests hang off it.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `CAP`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | user_facing \| background \| admin \| integration | `outlined` | Who or what experiences it. Decides whether it needs an entry point and which probes apply. |
| `tier` | enum | 1 \| 2 \| 3 | `outlined` | Criticality of this feature. |
| `owner` | string | text | `specified` | Who is accountable for it. |
| `facets` | shape | Yes/no characteristics that decide which probes apply. | `specified` | Yes/no characteristics that decide which probes apply. Derived ones may be left out; declared ones must be stated. |
| `probes` | shape | The disposition of every applicable concern probe: addressed, not applicable, or deferred. | optional | The disposition of every applicable concern probe: addressed, not applicable, or deferred. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose and value | `outlined` | all | Which user problem does this solve, what outcome should it achieve, what is the business value, and what is explicitly out of scope? |
| Entry conditions | `specified` | all | How is it reached? What must already be true: permissions, account or subscription state, data? What is the first thing a person sees? |
| Behaviour notes | `specified` | all | What happens that the flows, rules and states do not already say: concurrency, duplicate requests, partial completion, edge cases? |
| Release and maintenance | `specified` | 1, 2 | Flags, rollout, migration, monitoring, how to switch it off, and what retiring it would involve. |

### `SRF` Surface

A place where people or systems meet the product: web app, admin console, public API, email, marketing site.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `PROD`, `DOM`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | web_app \| mobile_app \| admin_console \| marketing_site \| docs_site \| public_api \| email \| webhook \| cli \| embedded_widget \| status_page \| other | `outlined` | What sort of surface it is. |
| `audience` | string | text | `outlined` | Who uses it. |
| `internal` | bool | true \| false | optional | True for staff-only surfaces. |
| `auth` | enum | required \| optional \| none | `specified` | Whether signing in is needed. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose | `outlined` | all | What is this surface for, and who uses it for what? |
| Navigation model | `specified` | all | How is it organised at the top level, and what are its entry points? |

## Experience

_How is it used, step by step?_

### `UC` Use case

A goal an actor wants to reach with the product, with its triggers and end states. Flows realise it.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `CAP`, `FEAT`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `goal` | string | text | `outlined` | What the actor wants to achieve, in one sentence. |
| `primary_actor` | ref | the id of a ACT or ROLE or PERS | `outlined` | Who wants it. |
| `supporting_actors` | refs | a list of ACT or ROLE or PERS ids | optional | Others who take part. |
| `trigger` | string | text | `specified` | What starts it. |
| `preconditions` | strings | a list: [item, item] | optional | What must be true before it can start. |
| `success` | text | text | `specified` | The state of the world when it has worked. |
| `failure` | text | text | `specified` | The acceptable end states when it does not work. |

### `JRN` Journey

An end-to-end experience across stages and touchpoints, from the person's point of view.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `PROD`, `DOM`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `persona` | ref | the id of a PERS or ACT | optional | Whose journey it is. |
| `outcome` | string | text | `outlined` | What the person has achieved at the end. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Narrative | `outlined` | all | Tell the journey as a story: where it starts, what the person wants at each stage and how it ends. |
| Pain points and opportunities | `specified` | all | Where does the experience hurt, and what would remove the friction? |

**Structured blocks**

| Block | Needed for | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pds-journey` | `specified` | stages: a list of {id, name, goal, actions, touchpoints, flows, feeling (1-5), pain, opportunity}. |

### `FLW` Flow

The exact sequence of steps and decisions that gets someone from a trigger to an end state, with every branch.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `CAP`, `FEAT`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | string | text | `outlined` | What starts the flow. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Notes | optional | all | Assumptions, variants and anything the steps do not say. |

**Structured blocks**

| Block | Needed for | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pds-flow` | `specified` | trigger, entry, steps. Each step has an id and one of next, decide, end or call; and optionally actor, at, does, uses, accesses, emits, moves. |

### `SCR` Screen

A page, dialog or panel where something happens, with the states it can be in.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `CAP`, `FEAT`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | page \| modal \| panel \| tab \| drawer \| wizard_step \| external_page | `outlined` | What sort of screen it is. |
| `route` | string | text | optional | Address or path, if it has one. |
| `data_bound` | bool | true \| false | `specified` | True when it shows data that can be loading, empty or wrong. |
| `states` | strings | a list: [item, item] | optional | The states that are defined, for example loading, empty, error, populated. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose | `outlined` | all | What is this screen for, and what does the person do here? |
| Content and states | `specified` | all | What is shown in each state, and what do the messages say? |
| Interactions | `specified` | all | What can the person do, what happens, and what feedback do they get? |
| Accessibility | `specified` | all | Keyboard use, screen-reader behaviour, focus order and how errors are announced. |

## Behaviour

_How must it behave?_

### `REQ` Requirement

One testable statement of what the product shall do or how well it shall do it.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `PROD`, `DOM`, `CAP`, `FEAT`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | functional \| quality \| constraint | `outlined` | functional: a behaviour. quality: how well, with a number. constraint: a limit imposed from outside. |
| `attribute` | enum | performance \| availability \| security \| privacy \| accessibility \| usability \| scalability \| observability \| compatibility \| localisation \| maintainability | optional | For quality requirements: which quality. |
| `statement` | text | text | `outlined` | One sentence, in the form: When <trigger>, the <system> shall <response>. See the authoring standards. |
| `priority` | enum | must \| should \| could | optional | How essential it is. |
| `verification` | enum | test \| inspection \| analysis \| demonstration | optional | How it will be shown to hold. |
| `verification_note` | string | text | optional | Required when verification is not test: how it will be shown. |

### `RULE` Business rule

A precise statement of how something is validated, calculated, limited or decided, with worked examples.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `PROD`, `DOM`, `CAP`, `FEAT`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | enum | validation \| calculation \| eligibility \| limit \| policy \| timing \| uniqueness \| ownership \| consistency | `outlined` | What sort of rule it is. |
| `statement` | text | text | `outlined` | The rule, exactly. |
| `examples` | shape | Worked examples: a list of {case, given, then}. | `specified` | Worked examples: a list of {case, given, then}. At least one positive and one negative or edge case. |
| `exceptions` | text | text | optional | Where the rule does not apply. |

### `STM` State machine

The states something can be in, how it moves between them, what causes each move and what each move triggers.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `DOM`, `CAP`, `FEAT`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | enum | entity \| process | `outlined` | entity: the lifecycle of a record. process: the progress of an activity. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Notes | `outlined` | all | What lifecycle is this, and why do these states exist? |
| Edge cases | `specified` | all | Concurrent transitions, retries, timeouts, reversals and what happens when two things try to move it at once. |

**Structured blocks**

| Block | Needed for | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pds-states` | `specified` | states: list of {id, label, kind (initial, normal, terminal), note}. transitions: list of {from, to, on, by, guard, emits}. |

## Information

_What does it know, send and depend on?_

### `ENT` Entity

A business concept the product keeps information about. Its home is its owner: the system of record.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `DOM`, `CAP`.

| `pii` | bool | true \| false | `specified` | True when any attribute is personal data. |
| `monetary` | bool | true \| false | optional | True when it holds money values or moves money. |
| `tenant_scoped` | bool | true \| false | `specified` | True when each record belongs to one tenant. |
| `system_of_record` | enum | internal \| external \| shared | `specified` | Who holds the authoritative copy. |
| `retention` | string | text | `specified` | How long it is kept and what then happens to it. |
| `has_lifecycle` | bool | true \| false | `specified` | True when records move through states that matter. |

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meaning | `outlined` | all | What is this concept in business terms, and how does it differ from similar ones? |
| Ownership and lifecycle | `specified` | all | Who creates and changes it, what happens when it is deleted, and how long is it kept? |

| Block | Needed for | Contents |

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |

### `API` API

A programmatic interface: a REST or GraphQL API, a webhook, an SDK or a command line. The contract itself lives elsewhere.

Adoption: `standard`. Lives under: `CAP`, `FEAT`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | enum | rest \| graphql \| webhook \| sdk \| cli | `outlined` | What sort of interface. |
| `audience` | enum | public \| partner \| internal | `outlined` | Who may use it. |
| `versioning` | string | text | `specified` | How versions are named and how long old ones live. |
| `auth` | string | text | `specified` | How callers authenticate. |
| `contract` | string | text | `specified` | Where the machine-readable contract lives: an OpenAPI or AsyncAPI path or address. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose | `outlined` | all | What can callers do with it, and who is it for? |
| Compatibility and deprecation | `specified` | all | What counts as a breaking change, how are changes announced, and how are old versions retired? |
| Limits | `specified` | all | Rate limits, quotas, pagination, idempotency and size limits. |

A third party the product depends on or exchanges data with: a payment provider, an identity provider, an email service.

| `status_page` | string | text | optional | Where its availability is published. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |

How the product and one external system exchange data: direction, protocol, what flows, what fails and how it recovers.

| `trial_days` | int | a whole number | optional | Length of a free trial, if any. |
| `entitlements` | shape | A list of {entl, value}: what the plan includes. | `specified` | A list of {entl, value}: what the plan includes. |

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |

Something a plan grants or limits: access to a feature, a quota or a rate.

## Measurement and operations

| `unit` | string | text | `specified` | The unit: count, percent, seconds, EUR. |

## Change and evidence

_What did we decide, assume, ask, learn and ship?_

### `DEC` Decision

A choice that was made, with the options considered and the consequences accepted.

Adoption: `core`. Lives under: `PROD`, `DOM`, `CAP`, `FEAT`.

**Fields**

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | enum | proposed \| accepted \| superseded \| rejected | `outlined` | Where the decision stands. |
| `date` | date | YYYY-MM-DD | `outlined` | When it was made (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `deciders` | strings | a list: [item, item] | `outlined` | Who decided. |

**Sections**

| Heading | Needed for | Tiers | The question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Context | `outlined` | all | What forced a choice, and what constraints applied? |
| Options considered | `specified` | all | At least two real options, each with what it costs and what it gains. |
| Decision | `outlined` | all | What was chosen, in one clear sentence. |
| Consequences | `specified` | all | What becomes easier, what becomes harder, and what must now be true? |

### `ASM` Assumption

Something taken to be true without proof, with what breaks if it is wrong and how it will be tested.

| Field | Type | Takes | Needed for | Meaning |

| `if_wrong` | string | text | `outlined` | What breaks if it is false. |

Something that must be answered before part of the definition can be trusted.
